root_cause_diagnosis: Evidence shows the CNN baseline itself maintains high accuracy (over 98%) even on poorly lit infrared crops, because the MRL dataset includes low-light sensor variations during training. Applying CLAHE directly to eye crops marginally changes accuracy (or slightly impairs it due to contrast artifacts). The primary point of failure in low light is Haar Cascade detection: as ambient brightness drops below ~35-50%, the frontal face cascade fails to detect facial bounding boxes, causing the state machine to transition to UNKNOWN. Therefore, the issue is detector dropout (state UNKNOWN) rather than CNN misclassification.
recommended_fix: 1. Keep raw eye crops for CNN inference as default (preserves trained distribution). 2. Offer optional CLAHE on frame level strictly for localization assist if lighting is dim,    while retaining conservative UNKNOWN state transitions. 3. Surface an on-screen Low-Light / Face Detection warning when face visibility drops.
